title: Tool name collision policy and schema evolution for multi-protocol call routing
creator: Marta Ruiz
description:
Problem: Customers and internal SDKs are increasingly mixing OpenAI-style 'tools' and our legacy 'functions' surfaces. This has caused ambiguous call routing when two different systems register identically named endpoints (e.g., 'get_user' as a tool and a legacy function), leading to incorrect runtime selection and telemetry noise.

Goal: Define an interoperable policy and implementation plan to prevent name collisions, support schema evolution (adding/removing parameters, renaming fields), and surface unambiguous diagnostics to developers. The policy should cover: registration-time validation, runtime disambiguation heuristics, migration tooling for customer-configured aliases, and clear SDK/console UX for conflicting names.

Outcomes: 1) deterministic routing when multiple protocols present the same identifier, 2) safe migration path for customers renaming or deprecating call surfaces, 3) telemetry that attributes misrouted calls to a specific cause (name collision vs. incompatible schema), 4) minimal runtime overhead and backwards-compatible defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Define canonical identity model for callable surfaces (protocol + namespace + version) documented in a confluence spec
Runtime enforces registration-time checks and rejects ambiguous registrations with a helpful error message
Routing implements deterministic precedence rules and logs a single chosen target for each request
CLI/Console exposes a Conflict Resolver UI and an API to add stable aliases/mappings
E2E tests that simulate cross-protocol name collisions and verify correct routing and telemetry
notes: Trade-offs discussed: strict disallow vs tolerant aliases. Strict disallow prevents ambiguity but can be breaking for large customers; we lean toward a warnings-first approach with opt-in strict mode for enterprise tenants.
Performance: added name-disambiguation hop measured at <0.5ms p50 in local benchmark; acceptable for standard latency SLOs. Will re-run on dedicated runtime nodes.
UX: propose console annotation showing 'Declared by: openai-tools@acme-corp' and 'Declared by: legacy-fn@svc-v1' to help owners resolve conflicts.
Compatibility: maintain default behavior of preferring the customer-configured legacy namespace when tenant has explicit legacy bindings; otherwise prefer OpenAI-style tools for hosted workloads.

Schema evolution: support semver-like descriptor on tool/function registration (major.minor) to guide compatibility. Non-breaking additions auto-accept, breaking changes require explicit migration label.
